subject: Incident notification framework / evidence access — DPA discussion
messages:
From: Simon Larsen <simon.larsen@nordicbank.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: NordicBank Legal <legal@nordicbank.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Mar 2027 08:12:00 -0500
Subject: Incident notification: clarifying timelines & evidence access under DPA

Rishi,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our DPA review the legal team has flagged two items that need firm language before we can proceed:

1) Notification timeline: our standard is notification of a confirmed material breach within 24 hours of becoming aware, with an initial description and mitigation steps.
2) Evidence access & exports: for regulatory audits we require timely copy of relevant logs, sample records, and an evidence package (redacted where appropriate). We need clarity on how quickly Redwood can provide that and the format/mechanism (SFTP, secure share, or on-prem retrieval).

Also: subprocessors. We need an explicit commitment about notification when a subprocessor causes or is implicated in an incident that affects NordicBank data, and whether we will provide contact details and relevant contractual flow-down.

Happy to hop on a short call if that helps — legal is flexible but wants concrete SLA language to avoid open-ended obligations.

Simon
Head of Information Security
NordicBank

--
Attachment: incident_clarifying_questions.xlsx (spreadsheet of specific asks)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Simon Larsen <simon.larsen@nordicbank.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Mar 2027 10:34:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Incident notification: clarifying timelines & evidence access under DPA

Hi Simon — thanks for the clear note. Quick responses below, then a proposed compromise you can run past legal.

1) Notification timeline: Redwood can commit to an initial acknowledgement to the named security contact within 24 hours of confirmed material impact. We propose an initial incident report (root-cause hypothesis + immediate mitigations) within 72 hours, and a follow-up with a final report and lessons learned within 30 days. We push back on a guaranteed full investigation within 24 hours because many vendor-side investigations require log consolidation and subprocessor cooperation.

2) Evidence access: Redwood can provide a curated evidence package (logs, sample records, AO-annotated timeline) delivered via a secure, access-controlled Share link or SFTP within 30 calendar days of request for most incidents. For high-priority regulatory audits where NordicBank certifies urgency, we will accelerate to 7 calendar days where operationally feasible, subject to data minimization and legal process (NDAs/Type of request). Large exports may require coordinated transfer windows to protect other customers and maintain performance.

3) Subprocessors: we will notify NordicBank within 48 hours when a subprocessor is materially implicated and share the subprocessor name, role, and remediation steps. We will enforce contractually required flow-down obligations and provide copies of the subprocessor contract summary on request.

I attached a short DPA paragraph bundle (DPA_Incident_Proposals_Redwood_v2.pdf) showing the proposed wording the legal team can redline. If that looks workable, Naomi or Lauren can take the redlines and convert to contract language.

If helpful, happy to do a 30-minute call next week to walk through edge cases (multinational data transfers, law enforcement requests).

Best,
Rishi
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Simon Larsen <simon.larsen@nordicbank.com>

Date: Sat, 06 Mar 2027 09:01:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Incident notification: clarifying timelines & evidence access under DPA

Rishi,

Thanks — that framing helps. A couple follow-ups from legal:

- The 72/30 split is reasonable as a starting point but legal wants explicit language on what constitutes a "confirmed" material impact (e.g., exposure of plaintext PII, unauthorized exfiltration of production datasets). Can you add a definitional paragraph?

- Evidence exports: 30 days is long for some regulatory bodies. They asked whether Redwood has an "emergency export" path for EU regulators (GDPR supervisory authorities) on a certified request, or if we would support direct handover to an auditor appointed by NordicBank.

- Cross-border transfers: because NordicBank's data is EU customer data, we need visibility into any transfers outside the EU and whether Redwood relies on SCCs or adequacy decisions for subprocessors. Please confirm the mechanism.

If you prefer, I can share a redline from legal after we incorporate your DPA paragraph.

Simon

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Simon Larsen <simon.larsen@nordicbank.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 11:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Incident notification: clarifying timelines & evidence access under DPA

Simon — looping in from Legal. We reviewed Rishi's proposed paragraph and drafted three short additions that should address the points below. Summary:

1) Definition of Confirmed Material Impact — we propose the following sentence to insert in the DPA: "A 'Confirmed Material Impact' means a security event that, following Redwood's preliminary assessment, reasonably appears to have resulted in unauthorized access to or exfiltration of personal data or a material interruption to data availability for the Customer's environment."

2) Emergency exports / auditor access — we can support auditor access under two tracks: (a) NordicBank-designated auditor with a mutually-agreed scope and NDA and (b) regulator-certified request where Redwood will work with the regulator to provide exports within a 7 business day window where technically feasible. We'll require specificity of scope and a formal request workflow to prevent overbroad collection.

3) Cross-border transfers & subprocessors — Redwood confirms it relies on EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) for transfers to non-adequate jurisdictions and will maintain an up-to-date subprocessor map. We will notify NordicBank within 10 business days of onboarding any new subprocessor that handles NordicBank data, and sooner in the event of a security event implicating that subprocessor.

We attached a short CSV export of current subprocessors for your team to review. If these three items look acceptable, we can prepare a redline to the main DPA and circulate for signature.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 09 Mar 2027 16:45:00 -05:00
Subject: RE: Incident notification: clarifying timelines & evidence access under DPA — agreed next steps

Simon / team — thanks for the quick turn. Per Lauren's note, here's the agreed summary and immediate next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

Agreed points:
- Initial acknowledgement: within 24 hours of Confirmed Material Impact.
- Initial incident report: within 72 hours. Final report and lessons learned: within 30 days.
- Evidence access: standard curated package within 30 calendar days; emergency/regulator-certified exports or auditor handover with signed NDA within 7 business days where feasible.
- Subprocessor notice: Redwood will notify within 48 hours if a subprocessor is materially implicated; we will also provide 10 business day notice of new subprocessors handling NordicBank data.
- Cross-border transfers: Redwood will rely on SCCs for transfers to non-adequate countries; details in the attached DPA paragraph.

Action items:
- Redwood (Lauren / Naomi): produce a redline to NordicBank's DPA incorporating the agreed language by COB Friday, 2027-03-12.
- NordicBank (Simon / Legal): review redline and flag any residual hard stops; propose meeting if required.
- Ops playbook: Naomi to prepare a short internal ops checklist for emergency evidence exports and escalation contacts.

I'll drop the redline and DocuSign link once Legal finishes the edit. Thanks again for the pragmatic approach — appreciate the focus on concrete SLAs that map to operational controls.

Best,
Rishi
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
